verdict.rationale: SumUp's first-party docs list Reader SDKs as an in-person integration path that embeds payment acceptance directly in Android or iOS apps. The app controls a card reader over Bluetooth or uses Tap to Pay, and the SDK docs also cover offline store-and-forward transactions. missing for 10: SDK-level documentation (installation, API reference, platform versions) and independent or hands-on corroboration of the mobile SDKs.

support.subject: As a developer, I can embed in-person payments into my own iOS or Android app with official mobile SDKs

citations.quote: Embed payment acceptance directly in your Android or iOS app. Your app controls the reader over Bluetooth or uses Tap to Pay.
There are three ways to integrate SumUp in-person payments: | | Cloud API | Reader SDKs | Payment Switch |
Mobile apps that need more control over the payment flow and user experience.
In this store-and-forward flow, card data is captured and cached securely on the device, then uploaded later for processing and authorization.
